subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Rise of Express Delivery
description: One-minute skill: The Rise of Express Delivery.

hook.text: In 1973, FedEx flew 389 packages on its first night. The idea: guarantee overnight delivery, anywhere.

buildup.text: Express delivery created a new market—businesses willing to pay a premium for guaranteed speed.

discovery.text: FedEx built a hub-and-spoke model. Every package flew through Memphis, then out to its destination.

twist.text: UPS countered with ground express. DHL dominated internationally. Speed became a three-way race.

climax.text: Express delivery turned logistics from invisible plumbing into a customer-facing brand experience.

punchline.text: Speed used to be a luxury. Now it's the expectation.

quiz.question: What logistics model did FedEx pioneer?
